**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS. Each question carries 25 marks.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.

Question 4(c) : tableau à compléter ; réponse attendue (usuelle dans les manuels) : vache = beef (boeuf) / suet ou dripping ; porc = pork / lard ; mouton = mutton / mutton fat ou tallow. questions.enonce_markdown: Name three (3) types of milk found in our markets. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Three types of milk found in the markets.**

1. Fresh milk (whole milk).
2. Powdered (dried) milk.
3. Evaporated milk.

(Other acceptable answers: sweetened condensed milk, skimmed milk, long-life (UHT) milk.)

questions.enonce_markdown: List eight (8) rules to follow when baking cake. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Eight rules to follow when baking a cake.**

1. Read the recipe and collect all the ingredients and equipment before starting.
2. Weigh and measure the ingredients accurately.
3. Use fresh ingredients of good quality, and have the fat and eggs at room temperature.
4. Grease and line the cake tin before mixing, and heat the oven to the right temperature beforehand.
5. Sieve the flour (with the baking powder) to add air and remove lumps.
6. Cream the fat and sugar until the mixture is light, pale and fluffy.
7. Add the beaten eggs a little at a time, beating well, so that the mixture does not curdle.
8. Fold in the flour gently with a metal spoon so as not to lose the air, then bake in the middle of the oven and do not open the oven door early.

(Also acceptable: test with a skewer or a light touch to see that the cake is cooked, and cool the cake on a wire rack.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following table:

| Animal | Meat | fat |
|---|---|---|
| Cow | ------- | ------- |
| ------- | ------- | lard |
| ------- | Mutton | ------- |

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Completed table.**

|---|---|---|
| Cow | Beef | Suet (or beef dripping) |
| Pig | Pork (also bacon and ham) | Lard |

There are six blanks, each worth one mark: beef, suet or dripping; pig, pork; sheep, mutton fat or tallow.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain briefly the effects of heat on fats. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Effects of heat on fats.**

1. Solid fats melt and become liquid when heated, for example lard and butter.
2. Fat can be heated to a much higher temperature than water, which makes frying possible.
3. If heating continues, the fat starts to smoke at its smoking point: it breaks down into glycerol and fatty acids, and a blue smoke with an unpleasant, irritating smell is given off.
4. Overheated fat darkens and burns, giving a bitter taste to food, and it may catch fire.
5. Fat heated again and again deteriorates: it becomes darker, thicker and less able to be used for frying.

questions.enonce_markdown: List three (3) types of informal food services. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Three types of informal food service.**

1. Buffet service (guests help themselves from a table and eat standing or seated).
2. Tray service (a meal is served on a tray, for example to a person in bed).
3. Self-service (cafeteria), where customers take their meal from a counter and carry it to the table.

(Other acceptable answers: counter service, snack-bar service, trolley service.)
